newsitem.title: RUSSIA: IMF board to consider Russia loan on Friday.
newsitem.headline: IMF board to consider Russia loan on Friday.

text.p: The board of the International Monetary Fund, which is backing Russian reforms with a $10 billion three-year loan, will meet on Friday to discuss resuming the loan programme, officials said on Wednesday.

IMF chief representative Martin Gilman said the meeting was likely to pave the way for Russia receiving new IMF funds. "Normally after board consideration Russia would become eligible to make the first drawing under the 1997 programme," he said.
IMF officials had already said the board would review the Russia programme on May 16.

The IMF, which assessed Russia's economic performance each month under the first year of the three-year loan, delayed several monthly payments this year and last year because it was worried about Moscow's ability to raise tax revenue.
But officials agreed to switch to quarterly monitoring this year and the board will consider the release of the first quarterly tranche of the 1997 programme on Friday.
It is for a total of 500 million Special Drawing Rights, currently worth around $690 million.
Gilman said the next IMF mission under the new system of quarterly monitoring was due to arrive in Moscow in the second half of July.
